items.q: A 24-year-old trauma patient suffers blunt abdominal injury. Fractures of which ribs on the left side are most commonly associated with laceration of the underlying spleen?
o: Left ribs 11 and 12 floating ribs only
items.exp: The spleen lies in the left hypochondrium directly protected by the lateral curves of the left 9th, 10th, and 11th ribs. Fractures here frequently lacerate the splenic parenchyma.
r: Correct. Fractures of left ribs 9 to 11 are most strongly associated with traumatic splenic injury.
Incorrect. Ribs 1-3 injuries correlate with aortic or subclavian vessel trauma.
Incorrect. Ribs 5-7 overlie the heart and left lung base.
Incorrect. Ribs 11-12 overlie the left kidney posteriorly.
items.kp: Fractures of the left 9th through 11th ribs place the underlying spleen at high risk for parenchymal laceration.

items.q: During splenectomy for severe trauma, ligation of short gastric vessels within the gastrosplenic ligament risks ischemic injury to which part of the stomach?
items.exp: Short gastric arteries run within the gastrosplenic ligament from the splenic artery to supply the gastric fundus. Aggressive dissection can compromise fundic vascularity.
r: Correct. Short gastric vessels supply the gastric fundus within the gastrosplenic ligament.
Incorrect. Gastric antrum is supplied by gastroepiploic and right gastric vessels.
Incorrect. Pylorus is supplied by right gastric and gastroduodenal branches.
Incorrect. Lesser curve is supplied by left gastric artery.
items.kp: The gastrosplenic ligament contains the short gastric arteries supplying the fundus of the stomach.

items.q: During mobilization of the splenic hilum, which anatomical organ is in direct intimate contact with the splenic vessels in the splenorenal ligament and vulnerable to iatrogenic transection?
items.exp: The tail of the pancreas lies within the splenorenal ligament and frequently abuts or enters the splenic hilum, creating a high risk of pancreatic fistulas if clamped during splenectomy.
r: Correct. The pancreatic tail lies in the splenorenal ligament abutting the splenic hilum.
Incorrect. Left suprarenal gland lies retroperitoneal medial to the kidney.
Incorrect. Duodenojejunal flexure is located medial to the midline.
Incorrect. Splenic flexure lies inferiorly, attached by phrenicocolic ligament.
items.kp: The tail of the pancreas lies within the splenorenal ligament and is vulnerable to iatrogenic injury during splenic hilar ligation.

items.q: In splenic histology, what is the primary immunological function of the periarteriolar lymphoid sheath (PALS) surrounding central arterioles?
o: Houses T lymphocytes for cellular immune surveillance
Filters aged non-deformable red blood cells
items.exp: In the white pulp, the periarteriolar lymphoid sheath (PALS) is composed predominantly of T lymphocytes wrapped around central arterioles, mediating cellular immune surveillance.
r: Correct. PALS is the T-cell compartment of splenic white pulp.
Incorrect. Filtering non-deformable erythrocytes is the function of the red pulp.
Incorrect. Platelet storage occurs in red pulp sinuses.
Incorrect. Opsonizing antibody synthesis occurs in B-cell follicles.
items.kp: The periarteriolar lymphoid sheath (PALS) in splenic white pulp is populated predominantly by T lymphocytes.

items.q: A post-splenectomy patient is at lifelong risk for overwhelming postsplenectomy infection (OPSI). Which encapsulated bacterium is the most common cause of fatal post-splenectomy sepsis?
items.exp: Streptococcus pneumoniae accounts for over 50-70% of all cases of overwhelming post-splenectomy sepsis, followed by Neisseria meningitidis and Haemophilus influenzae.
r: Correct. Streptococcus pneumoniae is the leading culprit in overwhelming post-splenectomy infection.
Incorrect. E. coli is not an encapsulated organism relying primarily on splenic opsonin clearance.
Incorrect. Pseudomonas causes opportunistic hospital-acquired infections.
Incorrect. Staph aureus causes soft tissue and catheter sepsis.
items.kp: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most frequent and lethal pathogen in overwhelming postsplenectomy infection (OPSI).

items.q: Examination of a peripheral blood smear from a patient three months after splenectomy reveals small, round basophilic nuclear inclusions within erythrocytes. What are these inclusions?
items.exp: Howell-Jolly bodies are nuclear DNA remnants normally removed by splenic macrophages in the cords of Billroth ('pitting'). Their presence indicates asplenia or hyposplenism.
r: Correct. Howell-Jolly bodies are nuclear remnants that persist after splenectomy.
Incorrect. Heinz bodies are precipitated hemoglobin clumps seen in G6PD deficiency.
Incorrect. Basophilic stippling represents ribosomal RNA aggregates seen in lead poisoning.
Incorrect. Pappenheimer bodies are iron-containing granules.
items.kp: Howell-Jolly bodies are nuclear remnants normally removed by splenic pitting, serving as a diagnostic hallmark of asplenia.

items.q: To re-enter the general venous circulation from the cords of Billroth, circulating erythrocytes must physically squeeze through 2-micrometer endothelial slits in which red pulp structures?
items.exp: Erythrocytes in the red pulp cords of Billroth must deform through narrow 2-micrometer clefts between barrel stave endothelial cells to enter venous sinusoids.
r: Correct. Erythrocytes must squeeze through narrow endothelial slits lining splenic venous sinusoids.
Incorrect. Central arterioles deliver blood into the white pulp.
Incorrect. Trabecular arteries are muscular conducting branches.
Incorrect. Marginal sinus surrounds follicles.
items.kp: Splenic sinusoids test erythrocyte deformability as red cells squeeze through narrow endothelial slits from cords of Billroth.

items.q: Which ligament provides an inferior horizontal shelf supporting the lower pole of the spleen, often requiring division to mobilize the splenic flexure of the colon?
items.exp: The phrenicocolic ligament extends from the splenic flexure of the colon to the diaphragm, serving as the anatomical floor (sustentaculum lienis) supporting the spleen.
r: Correct. The phrenicocolic ligament supports the inferior splenic pole.
Incorrect. Gastrosplenic carries short gastric arteries.
Incorrect. Splenorenal carries splenic vessels and pancreatic tail.
Incorrect. Falciform attaches liver to anterior wall.
items.kp: The phrenicocolic ligament (sustentaculum lienis) forms an anatomical shelf supporting the spleen.

items.q: A child with hereditary spherocytosis experiences recurrent hemolytic anemia and splenomegaly. Why are spherocytic erythrocytes prematurely destroyed in the spleen?
o: Spherical erythrocytes lack deformability and are trapped in the cords of Billroth
Spherocytes trigger massive antibody production in white pulp
Defective spectrin stimulates Kupffer cell phagocytosis
items.exp: Hereditary spherocytosis reduces membrane surface area-to-volume ratio, making red cells rigid spheres. They cannot deform through the 2-micrometer slits into sinusoids and are engulfed by cord macrophages.
r: Correct. Inflexible spherocytes cannot traverse sinusoidal slits and are phagocytosed in splenic cords.
Incorrect. Hemolysis in spherocytosis is mechanical entrapment, not antibody-mediated.
Incorrect. Kupffer cells are in the liver; splenic macrophages clear spherocytes.
Incorrect. Sinusoidal endothelium is a passive physical sieve.
items.kp: Rigid spherocytes in hereditary spherocytosis fail the splenic deformability test and are phagocytosed in cords of Billroth.

items.q: The splenic vein joins with which major vessel posterior to the neck of the pancreas to form the hepatic portal vein?
items.exp: The hepatic portal vein is formed posterior to the neck of the pancreas by the confluence of the splenic vein and the superior mesenteric vein.
r: Correct. The splenic vein and superior mesenteric vein join to form the portal vein.
Incorrect. Inferior mesenteric vein typically empties into the splenic vein earlier.
Incorrect. Left renal vein drains into IVC.
Incorrect. IVC is systemic venous circulation.
items.kp: The splenic vein unites with the superior mesenteric vein behind the pancreatic neck to form the hepatic portal vein.
